subject: AWS
one_line_core_task: Configure NACL inbound rules per subnet (HTTP, SSH, HTTPS from given ranges, deny rest); give rule tables and diagram. [printed BL=3]
question_text: A university hosts its student portal (vtop.vit.ac.in) and internal admin tools on AWS within a VPC containing two subnets: a public subnet (10.0.1.0/24) for the student portal and an admin subnet (10.0.2.0/24) for internal tools. To secure access, the network administrator must configure Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) such that the public subnet allows inbound HTTP traffic on port 80 from IP range 203.0.113.0/24 and SSH traffic on port 22 from 198.51.100.0/24, while the admin subnet allows only HTTPS traffic on port 443 from the campus admin network 192.0.2.0/24. All other inbound traffic to both subnets must be explicitly denied. How should the NACLs be configured to meet these requirements? Illustrate your answer with rule tables and diagram.
